hadith:
Transferance of a Debt from One Person to Another (Al-Hawaala) - Narrated Salama bin Al-Akwa:

Once, while we were sitting in the company of Prophet, a dead man was brought. The Prophet (ﷺ) was requested to lead the funeral prayer for the deceased. He said, "Is he in debt?" The people replied in the negative. He said, "Has he left any wealth?" They said, "No." So, he led his funeral prayer. Another dead man was brought and the people said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Lead his funeral prayer." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Is he in debt?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Has he left any wealth?" They said, ''Three Dinars." So, he led the prayer. Then a third dead man was brought and the people said (to the Prophet (ﷺ) ), Please lead his funeral prayer." He said, "Has he left any wealth?" They said, "No." He asked, "Is he in debt?" They said, ("Yes! He has to pay) three Diners.', He (refused to pray and) said, "Then pray for your (dead) companion." Abu Qatada said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Lead his funeral prayer, and I will pay his debt." So, he led the prayer.
message: The Prophet (ﷺ) emphasized the importance of fulfilling our financial obligations, even after death, reflecting Allah's justice and fairness in all matters. When we strive to be just and honor our debts, we align ourselves with Al 'Adl—The Just—and demonstrate trust in Allah's perfect wisdom. Let this be a reminder to settle our responsibilities with integrity, knowing that Allah sees all our actions and will judge us with perfect justice.
name:
Al 'Adl - الْعَدْلُ - The Just

The concept of Al 'Adl reflects the belief that Allah is just in His actions, laws, and decrees, ensuring fairness in the universe. This name emphasizes the importance of justice as a moral value in Islam, guiding individual behavior and societal laws. The origin of Al 'Adl is rooted in Islamic theology, where it underscores the belief that Allah does not oppress anyone and that all human beings will be judged fairly on the Day of Judgment.
